# Junction SCO baselines

The five `.sco` files were generated by `junction_sco_baseline_snapshots` on the
unmodified production code at integration commit `309ad4df93baf1ecf3c3876006bd1b2e4d716d87`.
The test fixture was temporarily included in that checkout and run with
`OPENMAPPER_SNAPSHOT_WRITE` pointing at this directory. It makes the three normal
junctions through `make_with` and places both pocket variants through the editor's
bus-pocket tool. The first taper in the direction of the original road is saved.
The regression test compares the complete SCO bytes, including the generated mesh
name and all path and helper records.

They were regenerated once more (same command, same fixture) on the merge of upstream
`v0.2.0` (`de21b085bb0b7811b3da85bba37d148fc6c1d1e6`): upstream's road markings now go
into the junction mesh (`plate_marks`/`add_marks`), so the mesh — and with it the
generated name, which is hashed from the mesh — changed. Only the `[friendlyname]` and
`[mesh]` lines differ; every `[splinehelper]` and `[path]` record is byte-for-byte the
same as before.

The three ordinary junction fixtures now describe the fixed 4 m approach/departure
policy for every turn. For their symmetric 18 m arms and 1.75 m lane offsets,
the remaining 90-degree arcs have radii 12.25 m (right) and 15.75 m (left).
The expected path records are calculated independently from these dimensions.
The derived mesh/friendly-name hashes alone are masked to zero by the snapshot
check; every other byte is checked. The two bus-bay fixtures retain their original
full-byte comparisons and are unchanged. Use OPENMAPPER_SNAPSHOT_WRITE to regenerate
these fixtures from the running Rust tests when changing the generation policy.
